explain.say: Before dawn on 25 June 1950, North Korean tanks rolled south across the 38th parallel, the line that had split Korea since 1945. Within three days they took Seoul. Look at the timeline. This was the first time the Cold War turned into a big hot war. Why would a line of latitude become a border?

explain.say: See the causes. Japan had ruled Korea from 1910; in 1945 the Soviet Union and the United States split it. Both Korean leaders, Kim Il-sung in the north and Syngman Rhee in the south, wanted to unite it. Soviet archives show Stalin approved Kim's invasion in spring 1950. Bruce Cumings stresses its civil-war roots. Which cause was local, and which global?

because.label: US signals
because.note: US troops left; Korea seemed outside US defence.

draw.answer: A civil war that superpowers turned international.

explain.say: Now the map. The Soviet Union was boycotting the UN Security Council, so the Council voted to defend South Korea. American-led UN forces were pushed into a small corner around Busan in the south-east. Then in September 1950 General MacArthur landed at Inchon near Seoul, behind North Korean lines. Why is landing behind an enemy so powerful?

Watch this graph of the front line, in degrees north, approximately. Down to the far south, then UN troops raced north towards the Chinese border. In October 1950 China sent hundreds of thousands of troops, pushing the UN back past Seoul. From 1951 the line stuck near the 38th parallel for two years. Can you see the yo-yo, then the flat line?

Look at the cost, all estimates: perhaps two million Korean civilians, and hundreds of thousands of soldiers from both Koreas, China and the UN side. The armistice of 27 July 1953 stopped the fighting, but no peace treaty was ever signed; a demilitarised zone still divides Korea. Careful work. Challenge: explain why historians call it the forgotten war.

draw.text: Estimates vary widely, especially for civilians and China.

faq.a: Korea had been divided at the 38th parallel in 1945, and both Korean governments wanted to unify it. Kim Il-sung invaded the South on 25 June 1950 with Stalin's approval and Mao's support. Historians like Bruce Cumings stress earlier civil conflict inside Korea.

faq.q: Why did China join the Korean War?
faq.a: When UN forces crossed the 38th parallel and advanced towards the Yalu River on China's border in October 1950, Mao feared a hostile American presence next door and sent hundreds of thousands of troops, called volunteers.
asks: When did China enter the Korean War?

faq.q: Did the Korean War ever end?
faq.a: Fighting stopped with the armistice signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953, but no peace treaty followed. North and South Korea remain divided by a heavily guarded demilitarised zone.

faq.q: Why did the UN fight in Korea?
faq.a: The UN Security Council voted to help South Korea in June and July 1950 while the Soviet Union was boycotting the Council over China's seat, so there was no Soviet veto. Sixteen countries sent combat troops, led by the United States.
asks: Which countries fought for the UN in Korea?

faq.a: On 15 September 1950 UN forces under General Douglas MacArthur landed at Inchon, near Seoul, far behind North Korean lines. It cut North Korean supply lines and led to the recapture of Seoul.

facts: North Korea invaded South Korea on 25 June 1950.
UN forces landed at Inchon on 15 September 1950.
The Korean armistice was signed on 27 July 1953.
